words.en: on the Himālaya, the snow mountain
words.g: m. loc. sg.; compound (see Samāsa)

sandhi.note: Final m becomes anusvāra before t; final t (voiced to d at word end, 8.2.39) becomes n before the nasal m of मे.
Visarga before c becomes s, then ś; च + अहम् → चाहम् (a + a → ā). The m of अहम् is anusvāra before y (8.3.23).

samasa.alt: Also analysed as a karmadhāraya with the middle member dropped, हिमयुक्तः अचलः ‘the snowy mountain’; the referent is the same.

morph.note: The name is given from the deed of 11.49: she who slew Durgama is called Durgā. As a word, दुर्ग (दुस् + √गम्, ‘hard to reach’) with the feminine -ā; the text connects it with the asura’s name, not with this etymology.
Past participle of वि + √ख्या, neuter to agree with नाम: ‘(that name) will become famous’.
Absolutive of √कृ with -त्वा: ‘having made (a form)’, i.e. assuming it. The clause it begins is completed in 11.51.

mantras.anvaya: ‘दुर्गा देवी’ इति तत् मे नाम विख्यातं भविष्यति। पुनः च यदा अहं हिमाचले भीमं रूपं कृत्वा (11.51: रक्षांसि भक्षयिष्यामि …)
mantras.anvaya_en: The first line closes the third descent: तत् मे नाम (subject) विख्यातं भविष्यति, with the name in an इति phrase. The second line opens a new यदा-clause (the fourth descent) whose verb is in 11.51.
mantras.lit: ‘Durgā Devī’ — thus that name of mine will become renowned. And again, when I, having assumed a terrible form on the Himālaya, —
mantras.tr: That name of mine, Durgā Devī, will be renowned. And again, when I take a terrible form on the Himālaya,
mantras.tr_note: The second line is the beginning of a sentence completed in 11.51–52.

comm.t: The third name of the same descent: having slain Durgama (11.49), the Goddess will be known as Durgā Devī. The second line opens the fourth descent: a terrible form on the Himālaya, completed in the next verse.

Here the text explains the name Durgā by a deed — the slaying of Durgama — not by the meaning ‘hard to approach’. The name has been used of her throughout the Devī Māhātmya; the prophecy gives it its story.
Lalitā Sahasranāma (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa) has दुर्गमा and दुर्गा as consecutive names, 189 and 190. The pairing is shared Śākta vocabulary; the Sahasranāma does not tell the story of Durgama.

sandhi.note: Final m becomes anusvāra before the consonant t. The same in मां मुनयः.
i before the unlike vowel ā becomes y.
Before a sibilant the visarga may stand; the text keeps it.

samasa.sense: for the sake of protecting (the sages)
samasa.alt: Also read as a karmadhāraya, त्राणम् एव कारणम् ‘protection being the reason’; the sense is the same.

morph.note: Future of √स्तु (aniṭ): guṇa स्तो + स्य, s → ṣ after o (स्तोष्य-), with -अन्ति. It recurs in 11.54.
Neuter plural of रक्षस्: the s-stem lengthens its vowel and inserts a nasal (anusvāra) before -सि in the nom./acc. plural.

mantras.anvaya: (यदा अहं हिमाचले भीमं रूपं कृत्वा) मुनीनां त्राणकारणात् रक्षांसि भक्षयिष्यामि, तदा सर्वे मुनयः आनम्रमूर्तयः (सन्तः) मां स्तोष्यन्ति,
mantras.anvaya_en: The first line completes the यदा-clause of 11.50 (verb भक्षयिष्यामि); the second is its correlative तदा-clause, whose sentence ends with the name in 11.52.
mantras.lit: — shall devour the rākṣasas for the protection of the sages, then all the sages, with bodies bowed low, will praise me;
mantras.tr: and devour the rākṣasas to protect the sages, then all the sages will bow low and praise me,
mantras.tr_note: The participial compound आनम्रमूर्तयः is rendered as a verb (‘bow low’). The sentence runs from 11.50 to 11.52.

comm.t: The fourth descent: on the Himālaya, in a terrible form, the Goddess devours rākṣasas to protect the sages, and the sages bow and praise her. The name follows in 11.52.
As in the third descent, the occasion is the sages’ need; each form in this prophecy is called down by a particular distress and named by those it saves.

sandhi.note: ā + a → ā (यदा + अरुण- → यदारुण-); visarga before t becomes s.
Final m becomes anusvāra before k.

morph.note: Future of √कृ (roots in ṛ take iṭ: कर् + इष्य + ति): ‘(he) will do, will cause’. With बाधाम्, ‘will cause affliction’.

mantras.anvaya: (तदा) ‘भीमा देवी’ इति तत् मे नाम विख्यातं भविष्यति। यदा अरुणाख्यः त्रैलोक्ये महाबाधां करिष्यति, (11.53: तदा अहं …)
mantras.anvaya_en: The first line closes the sentence of 11.50–51 with the name; the second opens the fifth descent with a यदा-clause whose correlative is in 11.53.
mantras.lit: ‘Bhīmā Devī’ — thus that name of mine will become renowned. When the one named Aruṇa causes great affliction in the three worlds, —
mantras.tr: and my name will be renowned as Bhīmā Devī. When the asura called Aruṇa brings great oppression on the three worlds,
mantras.tr_note: ‘Asura’ is supplied; the text gives only the name Aruṇa, but 11.53 calls him महासुरम्.

comm.t: The fourth form is named: Bhīmā Devī, ‘the Terrible Goddess’, from the terrible form of 11.50. The second line opens the fifth and last named descent: an asura called Aruṇa will afflict the three worlds.
The line ‘… इति विख्यातं तन्मे नाम भविष्यति’ is repeated word for word from 11.50, a formula that seals each naming. The repeated formula is how the prophecy keeps its shape as a list of names.

sandhi.note: ā + a → ā; the m of अहम् becomes anusvāra before bh (8.3.23).
ā + a → ā. The Gita Press writes an avagraha after the ā to show where the initial a of असंख्येय- was absorbed; it is a reading aid, not a separate sound.

samasa.type: bahuvrīhi (its members: असंख्येय, a nañ tatpuruṣa न संख्येयः; षट्पद, a bahuvrīhi षट् पादाः यस्य सः, ‘six-footed’ = bee)
samasa.literal: (a form) in which the six-footed ones are countless
samasa.sense: a form made of innumerable bees
for the good (of the three worlds)

morph.note: Taddhita with vṛddhi of the first syllable: भ्रमर → भ्रामर ‘belonging to bees, consisting of bees’. The feminine भ्रामरी becomes her name in 11.54.
Purāṇic future of the stem वध, as in 11.49.

mantras.anvaya: तदा अहं असंख्येयषट्पदं भ्रामरं रूपं कृत्वा त्रैलोक्यस्य हितार्थाय (तं) महासुरं वधिष्यामि।
mantras.anvaya_en: The correlative तदा-clause of 11.52: the absolutive phrase (… रूपं कृत्वा), the purpose (त्रैलोक्यस्य हितार्थाय), the verb वधिष्यामि and its object.
mantras.lit: — then I, having assumed a bee-form of countless six-footed ones, shall slay the great asura for the welfare of the three worlds.
mantras.tr: then I shall take a form of countless bees and slay that great asura for the good of the three worlds.

comm.t: The fifth descent: against Aruṇa the Goddess takes a form made of innumerable bees and kills him for the welfare of the three worlds. The form is a swarm, not a single body.

Later Śākta retellings, such as the Devī Bhāgavata Purāṇa, explain the form: Aruṇa had a boon that no two- or four-footed creature could kill him, so the Goddess came as six-footed bees. The Devī Māhātmya itself gives no reason for the form.
